architectural_implications.after: Generate eval and training corpora from a symbolic policy prior, using production only for transient inference and for insights fed back into the generator.
architectural_implications.before: Collect production data, curate it, and build eval/training sets from it over time.
architectural_implications.consequence: The eval dataset becomes a reproducible build artifact derived from policy version, so pipeline changes and policy changes must be versioned together.
architectural_implications.observation: Privacy constraints make real data retention structurally impossible, not merely expensive.

architectural_implications.after: A symbolic decision tree is the canonical artifact; the LLM reasons over it at inference and samples traces from it during generation.
architectural_implications.before: Policy lives in prompts and in human reviewers' heads; data generation prompts are written independently of the reasoning path.
architectural_implications.consequence: Updating policy must regenerate the corresponding data; drift between the symbolic tree and the real policy silently corrupts both accuracy and eval validity.
architectural_implications.observation: The policy representation becomes the shared source of truth for both runtime reasoning and data generation.

architectural_implications.after: The harness is generic and stable; each stage is a declarative skill authored by the domain expert.
architectural_implications.before: Engineers write bespoke pipeline code per document type; domain experts file requests.
architectural_implications.consequence: Requires a validation and review gate on skills themselves, since a bad skill is now a data-quality incident that no engineer gatekeeps.
architectural_implications.observation: Extension responsibility shifts from engineers to clinicians via skill files on a generic harness.

architectural_implications.after: Invariants, event sequence, document plans, and document text are separate stages with inspectable intermediate state.
architectural_implications.before: Single prompt asks the model to produce the entire artifact; failures surface only at the end.
architectural_implications.consequence: Adds stage boundaries where human-in-the-loop steering and per-stage evals can attach, at the cost of more orchestration and more places for inconsistency to creep in.
architectural_implications.observation: Generation is decomposed into layers with bounded per-step context instead of one monolithic prompt.

article_ideas.angle: Argue against treating a policy-derived generator as a neutral ground-truth substitute, and show the specific place where the loop closes: same artifact for runtime reasoning and for sampling the eval set.
article_ideas.audience: AI engineers and eval leads building in regulated domains
article_ideas.based_on: a symbolic form can act as a shared substrate
article_ideas.thesis: When the eval corpus and the system's reasoning scaffold are both derived from the same symbolic policy, the eval measures conformance to the encoding rather than fidelity to messy production reality; synthetic-heavy pipelines stay honest only if they reserve a channel for real, unmapped cases and report the coverage residual as a first-class metric.
article_ideas.title: Your Synthetic Eval Suite Is Grading the Policy, Not the World

article_ideas.angle: Frame mode collapse as a conditioning-design defect with a concrete remedy and a coverage-based success metric rather than a perceptual quality judgement.
article_ideas.audience: Applied ML engineers and data-generation practitioners
article_ideas.based_on: Instead of predicting outcomes from data (forward task)
article_ideas.thesis: Long-artifact synthetic data fails not because models are too weak but because the conditioning signal is too weak; inverting the task so the label and a sampled reasoning trace come first converts generation from a sampling-from-the-mode problem into a targeted branch-coverage problem, which is the only version of the task with a measurable acceptance criterion.
article_ideas.title: Don't Generate Documents, Generate the Decision First

article_ideas.angle: Reclassify a widely praised shortcut by its statistical role, and specify how to measure its precision against a reference standard.
article_ideas.audience: Teams replacing human labelling with automated verification
article_ideas.based_on: Round-trip checks between generated medical records and original task inputs
article_ideas.thesis: Automated inversion checks are valuable precisely because they are cheap and universal, but they measure recoverability, not realism; teams should treat them as a high-recall prefilter with a measured precision ceiling, budget a clinician adjudication sample on top, and stop reporting round-trip pass rate as if it were accuracy.
article_ideas.title: Round-Trip Is a Filter, Not a Metric

article_ideas.angle: Treat the harness/skill split as an organizational architecture with a governance gap, not just a nice developer-experience story.
article_ideas.audience: Platform architects and engineering managers in vertical AI
article_ideas.based_on: AI engineers should not own medical data pipelines
article_ideas.thesis: Putting domain experts in ownership of generation pipelines via declarative skills on a generic harness moves the extension bottleneck to exactly the right place, but it also deletes the engineering review gate on data quality; the pattern only works if skills themselves get a validation and review lifecycle, otherwise data-quality incidents get attributed to the model instead of the skill.
article_ideas.title: Who Is the Release Unit for a Data Pipeline?

connections.relationship: Inverting the supervised task turns the label from a prediction target into a conditioning input, which is what enables targeting rare decision branches.
The tree supplies both the branch structure for runtime reasoning and the sampler that guarantees each branch can be instantiated with a synthetic record.

connections.connects_to: evaluation pipelines without human ground truth
connections.relationship: Automated inversion-based verification substitutes for clinician labeling, which is the precondition for scaling to a synthetic-heavy corpus.

connections.concept: skills on a generic agent harness
connections.connects_to: human-in-the-loop steering at every generation stage
connections.relationship: Skill granularity defines the intervention points where clinicians can inject or correct generation without touching harness code.

connections.connects_to: synthetic data as the only durable dataset
connections.relationship: The legal inability to retain data forces generation to become the primary data-acquisition mechanism rather than a supplement to collected data.

evidence_quotes.text: Instead of predicting outcomes from data (forward task), the system samples an outcome label, generates a reasoning trace, and produces synthetic data backwards.
Starting from a sampled label and sampling a reasoning trace from policy allows generating data conditioned on diverse inputs.
Sampling reasoning traces from a symbolic causal representation provides a uniform and effective prior distribution.

core_insights.generalization: Applies to any synthetic data or eval-corpus generation where an LLM must produce long, structured artifacts with a known decision structure (underwriting, claims, compliance review, incident reports): invert the task and generate from the label down, not from a prompt up.
core_insights.insight: Invert the data pipeline: instead of predicting a label from a record, sample the outcome label first, then sample a reasoning trace from a symbolic policy representation, then generate the record backwards conditioned on that trace.
core_insights.why_it_matters: One-shot generation of long documents collapses to the average case; seeding generation with an explicit label plus a sampled reasoning path gives a controllable conditioning signal that can be targeted at specific outcomes and edge cases rather than the modal record.

evidence_quotes.text: Modeling policies as symbolic decision trees (similar to decision trees) improves accuracy and consistency scores in LLM workflows.
Symbolic representation enables deterministically sampling different reasoning traces for a given outcome.
Explicit policy modeling bridges the gap between unstructured medical rules and structured LLM execution.

core_insights.generalization: Wherever a business rule set exists in prose, a symbolic form can act as a shared substrate for both runtime reasoning and synthetic-data sampling, making the generator provably capable of hitting every branch of the decision space.
core_insights.insight: Encode domain policy as an explicit symbolic decision tree rather than leaving it implicit in prompts; this both improves LLM reasoning accuracy/consistency and provides a deterministic sampler over reasoning traces for any target outcome.
core_insights.why_it_matters: The same artifact serves two roles: an execution scaffold that constrains LLM reasoning, and a generator-side prior distribution. That collapses what are usually two separate systems (policy engine and prompt) into one representation.

evidence_quotes.text: Course-to-fine layering keeps prompt payloads token-efficient while scaling across longer patient journeys.
Patient invariants (biological sex, birth date, blood group) combined with reasoning traces generating ordered encounter events and document plans.
All generation and evaluation happen in the text domain using state-of-the-art PDF parsers and markdown text.

core_insights.generalization: Generalizes to any generation task whose output exceeds a comfortable context or attention budget: define an invariant layer, an event layer, and a rendering layer, and keep each step's conditioning small and inspectable.
core_insights.insight: Build long synthetic artifacts coarse-to-fine as a layer stack (patient invariants -> journey of events/encounters -> document plans per encounter -> document text), so each generation step has a small, bounded prompt payload.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Treats context length as a budget managed by decomposition rather than by larger windows; also creates natural checkpoints where a human or an eval can inspect and steer intermediate state before committing tokens to the next layer.

evidence_quotes.text: Round-trip checks between generated medical records and original task inputs ensure consistency and skip expensive ground-truthing processes.

core_insights.generalization: Any pipeline that generates artifacts from a known label can validate by inverting the generation and checking recoverability, trading human annotation cost for a computable proxy metric.
core_insights.insight: Use round-trip consistency checks (regenerate task inputs from the generated record, or verify record against the task input) as a cheap substitute for labeled ground truth in a synthetic data pipeline.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Ground-truthing by clinicians is the expensive bottleneck; a round-trip check turns dataset validation into an automated self-consistency test that can run on every sample, which is what makes a 90 percent synthetic corpus economically viable.

evidence_quotes.text: Pipelines modeled as skills running on a generic agent harness enable clinicians to add new document types without engineering changes.
AI engineers should not own medical data pipelines; domain experts know what is good and what is not.
Clinicians adding support for a new intake form by writing a new skill file attached to the pipeline.

core_insights.generalization: For vertical agents in regulated or expert-dominated domains, the harness/skill split makes the domain expert the release unit for pipeline changes instead of the engineering team.
core_insights.insight: Place pipeline ownership with domain experts by expressing each pipeline stage as a skill file running on a generic agent harness, so clinicians can add new document types without engineering changes.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Moves the extension boundary from code to declarative skill artifacts; the agent harness becomes stable infrastructure while domain knowledge is injected as data. This is a concrete answer to where domain expertise should live in an agentic system.

evidence_quotes.text: 90 percent of Anterior's datasets are synthetic, helping maintain a greater than 95 percent accuracy (F1) SLA in production.

core_insights.generalization: Suggests a prototype: measure whether a synthetic eval suite built from a symbolic policy prior ranks real production failures the same way a real-data suite does.
core_insights.insight: A production system reportedly operating on ~90 percent synthetic datasets claims a >95 percent F1 SLA in production.
core_insights.why_it_matters: If true, this is strong evidence that synthetic-only eval and training data can be sufficient in a domain with extreme accuracy requirements and near-zero real-data retention, reframing data scarcity as a generation-engineering problem rather than a collection problem.

evidence_quotes.text: Round-trip checks between generated medical records and original task inputs ensure consistency and skip expensive ground-truthing processes.

deep_dives.research_question: Does round-trip pass rate on generated artifacts correlate with human-adjudicated correctness strongly enough to use it as a dataset filter, and what is the precision of the filter at realistic operating thresholds?
deep_dives.topic: Round-trip consistency as a ground-truth proxy: validity, not just reliability
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Round-trip checks between generated medical records and original task inputs
deep_dives.why: If round-trip checks are only self-consistency with the generator, a 90% synthetic corpus can be perfectly verifiable and clinically implausible at the same time. Knowing the precision/reference-standard agreement of this check determines whether it can replace clinician adjudication or must be paired with a sampled human audit.

evidence_quotes.text: Sampling reasoning traces from a symbolic causal representation provides a uniform and effective prior distribution.
Starting from a sampled label and sampling a reasoning trace from policy allows generating data conditioned on diverse inputs.

deep_dives.research_question: What reweighting of the symbolic trace sampler is required so a synthetic corpus matches observed production outcome frequencies, and does a mismatched prior systematically misrank real production failures?
deep_dives.topic: Calibrating the label prior in reverse-inference generation
deep_dives.trigger_insight: What fraction of real-world edge cases fall outside the modeled symbolic decision space?
deep_dives.why: The pipeline as described samples from a uniform prior over traces, which by construction is not the production decision distribution. If eval rank ordering is sensitive to class balance, the whole synthetic eval suite's conclusions are a function of an arbitrary sampling choice rather than of model quality.

evidence_quotes.text: Modeling policies as symbolic decision trees (similar to decision trees) improves accuracy and consistency scores in LLM workflows.
Symbolic representation enables deterministically sampling different reasoning traces for a given outcome.

deep_dives.research_question: Can an automated differential test — re-derive traces from the tree and adjudicate each against the source policy text with an independent model or reviewer — detect policy-to-tree divergence before it corrupts both runtime accuracy and eval validity?
deep_dives.topic: Detecting drift between the symbolic policy tree and the authoritative prose policy
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How do you detect that the symbolic policy tree has drifted from the authoritative prose policy?
deep_dives.why: The symbolic tree is the shared source of truth for both inference and data generation, so a silent encoding error is not a bug in one component; it simultaneously degrades the model and invalidates the dataset that certifies it. Detecting that class of failure is a precondition for versioning policy and data together.

evidence_quotes.text: Most contracts prohibit retaining, reusing, or deriving information from PHI, preventing long-term persistence in data sets for evals.
Sampling reasoning traces from a symbolic causal representation provides a uniform and effective prior distribution.

deep_dives.research_question: What proportion of real production documents cannot be mapped onto any path of the symbolic tree, and does that residual concentrate in the rare-but-important cases the pipeline was built to capture?
deep_dives.topic: Coverage residual of the symbolic decision space
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How do you detect that the symbolic policy tree has drifted from the authoritative prose policy?
deep_dives.why: A generator that samples from an explicit tree can only instantiate branches the tree encodes; the long tail is systematically excluded by construction rather than randomly missed. Quantifying the unmapped residual turns an invisible exclusion into a measurable coverage metric and gives an upper bound on what synthetic data alone can validate.

project_ideas.based_on: Standard LLM prompting to generate 300-page medical records suffers from mode collapse
project_ideas.hypothesis: Sampling reasoning traces from an explicit symbolic decision tree yields measurably higher branch coverage and lower duplicate-record rate than direct prompting for diversity, at equal or lower token cost, for artifacts exceeding roughly 50 pages.
project_ideas.measurement: Branch coverage of the decision space, distinct-record rate / pairwise embedding similarity, human-rated plausibility, and total tokens per accepted record.
project_ideas.name: Trace-Prior Coverage Bench
project_ideas.poc: Take one prose rule set (e.g. a device-necessity review guideline), encode it as a decision tree, and generate N records two ways: (a) one-shot prompt asking for diverse records, (b) label sampling plus deterministic trace sampling plus backward generation. Hold model and token budget constant.

project_ideas.based_on: Round-trip checks between generated medical records and original task inputs
project_ideas.hypothesis: Round-trip consistency pass rate has a measurable precision ceiling as a correctness filter — a nontrivial fraction of round-trip-passing records are judged incorrect by domain adjudication — and that ceiling is stable enough to be reported as a constant in the pipeline's quality contract.
project_ideas.measurement: Precision/recall of round-trip check versus adjudication; fraction of round-trip-passing-but-adjudicated-wrong records; variance across generator versions.
project_ideas.name: Round-Trip Precision Audit
project_ideas.poc: Run round-trip checks and blinded domain-expert adjudication on the same 200-record batch from a label-conditioned generator; compute agreement, precision, and recall of the automated check against adjudication, then repeat on a batch drawn from a different generator to test stability.

project_ideas.based_on: How do you detect that the symbolic policy tree has drifted from the authoritative prose policy?
project_ideas.hypothesis: A differential test that samples traces from the symbolic tree and adjudicates each against the source prose policy with an independent model detects injected tree mutations at high recall, making policy-to-tree drift a catchable build-time failure rather than a silent production regression.
project_ideas.measurement: Mutation detection recall and false-positive rate per mutation class; reviewer agreement with the automated adjudicator; detection latency versus a no-test baseline.
project_ideas.name: Policy-Tree Drift Differential Tester
project_ideas.poc: Build a policy-to-tree extractor, then inject controlled mutations (dropped condition, flipped threshold, wrong branch order) into a known tree. Generate traces per mutation and have an independent model plus a human reviewer check each trace against the source text.

project_ideas.based_on: Course-to-fine layering keeps prompt payloads token-efficient
project_ideas.hypothesis: Coarse-to-fine layering (invariants, event sequence, document plans, text) produces equal or better cross-document consistency than monolithic generation at lower total token cost, and its intermediate state is inspectable enough that stage-level evals catch injected inconsistencies that end-to-end evals miss.
project_ideas.measurement: Total tokens per artifact, cross-document consistency score, detection rate of injected layer-local errors, and human intervention count per generation.
project_ideas.name: Layered Generator Harness with Per-Stage Eval Hooks
project_ideas.poc: Implement a four-stage generator with persisted intermediate state on an agent harness. Compare against a single-prompt generator for equivalent output length. Inject a factual inconsistency at the invariants layer and test whether stage-level checks catch it where end-to-end checks do not.

source.author: AI Engineer
source.title: Don’t be data poor — Anuj Iravane, Anterior

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Anuj Iravane
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Synthetic data generation and evaluation pipelines for healthcare administrative workflows using LLMs.
  • Purpose: To demonstrate how synthetic data generation combined with reasoning trace sampling, clinical policies as symbolic decision trees, and human-in-the-loop validation can solve the data scarcity problem in high-stakes healthcare administrative workflows. Anuj Iravane from Anterior discusses how clinician-led AI companies built for health plans face a major bottleneck: the data they most need (patient trajectories, complex medical records, unformatted faxes) is the data they are least allowed to keep due to PHI and strict contracting. To overcome this, Anterior reverses the inference workflow to synthetically generate medical records using policy-guided reasoning traces and symbolic decision trees, ensuring high accuracy and enabling domain experts to own the data pipeline.

Topic Map

The Healthcare Data Challenge

  • Explanation: Healthcare administrative workflows operate over unstructured data (faxes, handwritten medical notes, check boxes, key-value pairs) representing entire patient clinical trajectories, but privacy laws (PHI) and contracts prevent retaining or reusing this data.
  • Key claims:
    • Approximately 70 percent of medical communication still goes by fax.
    • Healthcare baseline accuracy requirements are exceptionally high (95 percent is not good enough).
    • Most contracts prohibit retaining, reusing, or deriving information from PHI, preventing long-term persistence in data sets for evals.
  • Examples:
    • Scanned fax bundles containing unstructured patient medical records, tables, and handwritten notes.
  • Terminology:
    • PHI
    • long tail
    • unstructured data
    • clinical trajectory
  • Why it matters: AI engineering in high-stakes domains requires massive, high-quality data for evals and fine-tuning, yet privacy constraints restrict data retention.

Reversing the Inference Workflow for Synthetic Data

  • Explanation: Instead of predicting outcomes from data (forward task), the system samples an outcome label, generates a reasoning trace, and produces synthetic data backwards.
  • Key claims:
    • Standard LLM prompting to generate 300-page medical records suffers from mode collapse and produces generic rather than specific data.
    • Starting from a sampled label and sampling a reasoning trace from policy allows generating data conditioned on diverse inputs.
    • Sampling reasoning traces from a symbolic causal representation provides a uniform and effective prior distribution.
  • Examples:
    • Sampling a CPAP medical necessity review outcome and generating the 300-page medical record backward.
  • Terminology:
    • mode collapse
    • synthetic data generation
    • reasoning trace
    • symbolic reasoning graph
  • Why it matters: Reversing inference helps overcome LLM mode collapse and generates diverse realistic edge cases for rigorous evals.

Clinical Policies as Symbolic Decision Trees

  • Explanation: Clinical policies (such as medical necessity review guidelines for CPAP devices) can be explicitly modeled as symbolic decision trees to improve LLM reasoning accuracy and consistency.
  • Key claims:
    • Clinical policies outline diverse conditions and decision logic for approvals or rejections.
    • Modeling policies as symbolic decision trees (similar to decision trees) improves accuracy and consistency scores in LLM workflows.
    • Symbolic representation enables deterministically sampling different reasoning traces for a given outcome.
  • Examples:
    • Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) medical necessity policy guidelines outlining diagnostic documentation requirements.
  • Terminology:
    • clinical policies
    • symbolic graphs
    • decision trees
    • medical necessity review
  • Why it matters: Explicit policy modeling bridges the gap between unstructured medical rules and structured LLM execution.

The Full Synthetic Data Pipeline

  • Explanation: Anterior's pipeline builds medical records layer by layer: patient invariants, patient journey (events and encounters), documents per encounter (plan, c&p, path report, discharge), and refinement via evals.
  • Key claims:
    • Course-to-fine layering keeps prompt payloads token-efficient while scaling across longer patient journeys.
    • Round-trip checks between generated medical records and original task inputs ensure consistency and skip expensive ground-truthing processes.
    • All generation and evaluation happen in the text domain using state-of-the-art PDF parsers and markdown text.
  • Examples:
    • Patient invariants (biological sex, birth date, blood group) combined with reasoning traces generating ordered encounter events and document plans.
  • Terminology:
    • patient journey
    • course-to-fine layering
    • round-trip check
    • skills-based workflow
  • Why it matters: Layered pipelines allow token-efficient generation and robust automated verification of complex synthetic medical histories.

Empowering Domain Experts with Skills and Human-in-the-Loop

  • Explanation: Domain experts (clinicians) should own the data pipeline by injecting ideas at each generation point and building skills-based workflows.
  • Key claims:
    • AI engineers should not own medical data pipelines; domain experts know what is good and what is not.
    • Human-in-the-loop mechanisms allow clinicians to steer generation at any point using production insights.
    • Pipelines modeled as skills running on a generic agent harness enable clinicians to add new document types without engineering changes.
  • Examples:
    • Clinicians adding support for a new intake form by writing a new skill file attached to the pipeline.
  • Terminology:
    • human in the loop
    • skills-based workflow
    • agent harness
    • domain experts
  • Why it matters: Placing domain experts in control ensures domain relevance, high data quality, and continuous pipeline improvement.

Key Points

70 percent of medical communication is faxed

  • Explanation: Medical data is extremely unstructured, consisting of scanned faxes, handwritten notes, and varied formats representing a patient's entire clinical trajectory.
  • Evidence: Mentioned as a key statistical challenge in healthcare communication.
  • Practical implication: AI systems must handle messy, unstructured, multi-modal medical documents rather than clean relational databases.

LLMs suffer from mode collapse when generating synthetic data

  • Explanation: Prompting an LLM to generate a 300-page medical record in one shot collapses diversity to the average case and fails to produce convincing edge cases.
  • Evidence: Described as the mode collapse problem when attempting one-shot synthetic record generation.
  • Practical implication: Synthetic generation needs structured decomposition (reverse inference) rather than simple one-shot prompts.

Synthetic data pipeline achieves high production accuracy

  • Explanation: 90 percent of Anterior's datasets are synthetic, helping maintain a greater than 95 percent accuracy (F1) SLA in production.
  • Evidence: Results slide showing production performance metrics.
  • Practical implication: Synthetic data pipelines can successfully substitute for retained PHI data in evaluating and testing complex AI workflows.

Clinicians cannot reliably distinguish synthetic data from real data

  • Explanation: In blind reviews, clinicians were only able to distinguish synthetic medical records from real ones approximately 60 percent of the time.
  • Evidence: Blind review results cited in the presentation results section.
  • Practical implication: Synthetic data generated via reverse inference is of high enough fidelity to pass expert clinical scrutiny.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Reverse Inference Synthetic Data Pipeline

  • How it works: Starts from a sampled outcome label and reasoning trace, then conditions the backward generation of medical records and patient journeys.
  • Components:
    • Sampled seed label
    • Symbolic reasoning trace
    • Patient invariants
    • Patient journey (events and encounters)
    • Document plans and document generation
    • Evals loop (consistency and realism round-trip checks)
  • When to use: When data is ephemeral, sensitive (PHI), expensive to label, or restricted by privacy contracts.

Examples & Case Studies

Anterior modeled CPAP medical necessity review policies as symbolic reasoning graphs/decision trees.

  • Illustrates: How complex clinical guidelines can be converted into deterministic symbolic representations for AI workflows.
  • Lesson: Symbolic reasoning graphs improve accuracy and consistency scores compared to raw LLM prompting.

Clinicians added support for a new intake form by writing a new skill file and attaching it to the pipeline.

  • Illustrates: Empowering domain experts to own the data pipeline without requiring software engineering changes.
  • Lesson: Skills-based architectures bridge the gap between AI engineers and domain experts.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Try reversing your inference workflow when data is restricted or scarce.
    • Ensure diversity is sampled from appropriate prior distributions rather than relying on one-shot LLM generation.
  • Strategic:
    • Emulate the actual process by which real-world data was generated.
    • Give domain experts the keys to own data pipelines through skills-based agent harnesses.
  • Questions to investigate:

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Approximately 70 percent of medical communication still goes by fax. (industry statistic)
  • In blind review, clinicians distinguished synthetic from real only less than 60 percent of the time. (empirical evaluation metric)
  • 90 percent of datasets used are synthetic, maintaining >95 percent accuracy (F1) SLA in production. (production performance metric)

Notable Quotes

"Anterior is a clinician-led AI company built for health plans, and backed by Sequoia and NEA." "What do you do when the data you most need is the data you're least allowed to keep?" "Synthetically generate it yourself." "In blind review, clinicians distinguished synthetic from real only <60 percent of the time."

Compressed Summary

  • Healthcare AI workflows rely on unstructured medical records that cannot be retained due to PHI and privacy contracts.
  • Reversing inference by sampling labels and reasoning traces backwards solves LLM mode collapse and data scarcity.
  • Clinical policies modeled as symbolic decision trees improve reasoning accuracy and consistency.

## Overview
- **Speaker**: Anuj Iravane
- **Channel**: AI Engineer
- **Main topic**: Synthetic data generation and evaluation pipelines for healthcare administrative workflows using LLMs.
- **Purpose**: To demonstrate how synthetic data generation combined with reasoning trace sampling, clinical policies as symbolic decision trees, and human-in-the-loop validation can solve the data scarcity problem in high-stakes healthcare administrative workflows.
Anuj Iravane from Anterior discusses how clinician-led AI companies built for health plans face a major bottleneck: the data they most need (patient trajectories, complex medical records, unformatted faxes) is the data they are least allowed to keep due to PHI and strict contracting. To overcome this, Anterior reverses the inference workflow to synthetically generate medical records using policy-guided reasoning traces and symbolic decision trees, ensuring high accuracy and enabling domain experts to own the data pipeline.
## Topic Map
### The Healthcare Data Challenge
- **Explanation**: Healthcare administrative workflows operate over unstructured data (faxes, handwritten medical notes, check boxes, key-value pairs) representing entire patient clinical trajectories, but privacy laws (PHI) and contracts prevent retaining or reusing this data.
- **Key claims**:
  - Approximately 70 percent of medical communication still goes by fax.
  - Healthcare baseline accuracy requirements are exceptionally high (95 percent is not good enough).
  - Most contracts prohibit retaining, reusing, or deriving information from PHI, preventing long-term persistence in data sets for evals.
- **Examples**:
  - Scanned fax bundles containing unstructured patient medical records, tables, and handwritten notes.
- **Terminology**:
  - PHI
  - long tail
  - unstructured data
  - clinical trajectory
- **Why it matters**: AI engineering in high-stakes domains requires massive, high-quality data for evals and fine-tuning, yet privacy constraints restrict data retention.
### Reversing the Inference Workflow for Synthetic Data
- **Explanation**: Instead of predicting outcomes from data (forward task), the system samples an outcome label, generates a reasoning trace, and produces synthetic data backwards.
- **Key claims**:
  - Standard LLM prompting to generate 300-page medical records suffers from mode collapse and produces generic rather than specific data.
  - Starting from a sampled label and sampling a reasoning trace from policy allows generating data conditioned on diverse inputs.
  - Sampling reasoning traces from a symbolic causal representation provides a uniform and effective prior distribution.
- **Examples**:
  - Sampling a CPAP medical necessity review outcome and generating the 300-page medical record backward.
- **Terminology**:
  - mode collapse
  - synthetic data generation
  - reasoning trace
  - symbolic reasoning graph
- **Why it matters**: Reversing inference helps overcome LLM mode collapse and generates diverse realistic edge cases for rigorous evals.
### Clinical Policies as Symbolic Decision Trees
- **Explanation**: Clinical policies (such as medical necessity review guidelines for CPAP devices) can be explicitly modeled as symbolic decision trees to improve LLM reasoning accuracy and consistency.
- **Key claims**:
  - Clinical policies outline diverse conditions and decision logic for approvals or rejections.
  - Modeling policies as symbolic decision trees (similar to decision trees) improves accuracy and consistency scores in LLM workflows.
  - Symbolic representation enables deterministically sampling different reasoning traces for a given outcome.
- **Examples**:
  - Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) medical necessity policy guidelines outlining diagnostic documentation requirements.
- **Terminology**:
  - clinical policies
  - symbolic graphs
  - decision trees
  - medical necessity review
- **Why it matters**: Explicit policy modeling bridges the gap between unstructured medical rules and structured LLM execution.
### The Full Synthetic Data Pipeline
- **Explanation**: Anterior's pipeline builds medical records layer by layer: patient invariants, patient journey (events and encounters), documents per encounter (plan, c&p, path report, discharge), and refinement via evals.
- **Key claims**:
  - Course-to-fine layering keeps prompt payloads token-efficient while scaling across longer patient journeys.
  - Round-trip checks between generated medical records and original task inputs ensure consistency and skip expensive ground-truthing processes.
  - All generation and evaluation happen in the text domain using state-of-the-art PDF parsers and markdown text.
- **Examples**:
  - Patient invariants (biological sex, birth date, blood group) combined with reasoning traces generating ordered encounter events and document plans.
- **Terminology**:
  - patient journey
  - course-to-fine layering
  - round-trip check
  - skills-based workflow
- **Why it matters**: Layered pipelines allow token-efficient generation and robust automated verification of complex synthetic medical histories.
### Empowering Domain Experts with Skills and Human-in-the-Loop
- **Explanation**: Domain experts (clinicians) should own the data pipeline by injecting ideas at each generation point and building skills-based workflows.
- **Key claims**:
  - AI engineers should not own medical data pipelines; domain experts know what is good and what is not.
  - Human-in-the-loop mechanisms allow clinicians to steer generation at any point using production insights.
  - Pipelines modeled as skills running on a generic agent harness enable clinicians to add new document types without engineering changes.
- **Examples**:
  - Clinicians adding support for a new intake form by writing a new skill file attached to the pipeline.
- **Terminology**:
  - human in the loop
  - skills-based workflow
  - agent harness
  - domain experts
- **Why it matters**: Placing domain experts in control ensures domain relevance, high data quality, and continuous pipeline improvement.
## Key Points
### 70 percent of medical communication is faxed
- **Explanation**: Medical data is extremely unstructured, consisting of scanned faxes, handwritten notes, and varied formats representing a patient's entire clinical trajectory.
- **Evidence**: Mentioned as a key statistical challenge in healthcare communication.
- **Practical implication**: AI systems must handle messy, unstructured, multi-modal medical documents rather than clean relational databases.
### LLMs suffer from mode collapse when generating synthetic data
- **Explanation**: Prompting an LLM to generate a 300-page medical record in one shot collapses diversity to the average case and fails to produce convincing edge cases.
- **Evidence**: Described as the mode collapse problem when attempting one-shot synthetic record generation.
- **Practical implication**: Synthetic generation needs structured decomposition (reverse inference) rather than simple one-shot prompts.
### Synthetic data pipeline achieves high production accuracy
- **Explanation**: 90 percent of Anterior's datasets are synthetic, helping maintain a greater than 95 percent accuracy (F1) SLA in production.
- **Evidence**: Results slide showing production performance metrics.
- **Practical implication**: Synthetic data pipelines can successfully substitute for retained PHI data in evaluating and testing complex AI workflows.
### Clinicians cannot reliably distinguish synthetic data from real data
- **Explanation**: In blind reviews, clinicians were only able to distinguish synthetic medical records from real ones approximately 60 percent of the time.
- **Evidence**: Blind review results cited in the presentation results section.
- **Practical implication**: Synthetic data generated via reverse inference is of high enough fidelity to pass expert clinical scrutiny.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Reverse Inference Synthetic Data Pipeline
- **How it works**: Starts from a sampled outcome label and reasoning trace, then conditions the backward generation of medical records and patient journeys.
- **Components**:
  - Sampled seed label
  - Symbolic reasoning trace
  - Patient invariants
  - Patient journey (events and encounters)
  - Document plans and document generation
  - Evals loop (consistency and realism round-trip checks)
- **When to use**: When data is ephemeral, sensitive (PHI), expensive to label, or restricted by privacy contracts.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Anterior modeled CPAP medical necessity review policies as symbolic reasoning graphs/decision trees.
- **Illustrates**: How complex clinical guidelines can be converted into deterministic symbolic representations for AI workflows.
- **Lesson**: Symbolic reasoning graphs improve accuracy and consistency scores compared to raw LLM prompting.
### Clinicians added support for a new intake form by writing a new skill file and attaching it to the pipeline.
- **Illustrates**: Empowering domain experts to own the data pipeline without requiring software engineering changes.
- **Lesson**: Skills-based architectures bridge the gap between AI engineers and domain experts.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Try reversing your inference workflow when data is restricted or scarce.
  - Ensure diversity is sampled from appropriate prior distributions rather than relying on one-shot LLM generation.
- **Strategic**:
  - Emulate the actual process by which real-world data was generated.
  - Give domain experts the keys to own data pipelines through skills-based agent harnesses.
- **Questions to investigate**:
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Approximately 70 percent of medical communication still goes by fax. (industry statistic)
- In blind review, clinicians distinguished synthetic from real only less than 60 percent of the time. (empirical evaluation metric)
- 90 percent of datasets used are synthetic, maintaining >95 percent accuracy (F1) SLA in production. (production performance metric)
## Notable Quotes
> "Anterior is a clinician-led AI company built for health plans, and backed by Sequoia and NEA."
> "What do you do when the data you most need is the data you're least allowed to keep?"
> "Synthetically generate it yourself."
> "In blind review, clinicians distinguished synthetic from real only <60 percent of the time."
## Compressed Summary
- Healthcare AI workflows rely on unstructured medical records that cannot be retained due to PHI and privacy contracts.
- Reversing inference by sampling labels and reasoning traces backwards solves LLM mode collapse and data scarcity.
- Clinical policies modeled as symbolic decision trees improve reasoning accuracy and consistency.
- Skills-based agent architectures empower clinical domain experts to own and extend the synthetic data pipeline.
- **Keywords**: synthetic data, healthcare ai, reasoning traces, symbolic graphs, evaluation pipelines
- **Core insight**: When privacy restrictions prevent retaining sensitive clinical data, reversing the inference workflow to synthetically generate medical records from symbolic policy trees enables high-accuracy AI evaluation and production success.
